Total Recall Bias is perhaps one of the most important things I've written and modeled during my career. @StateNavigate absolutely called it.

The industry will need to change how it uses recalled vote going forward; it is a double-edged sword: it was helpful in 2024, but it was poison in 2026. @Nate_Cohn at NYT/Siena used synthetic recalled vote, and it helped them greatly this year.

🚨NEW ARTICLE AND INTERACTIVES🚨

Polling has a problem this year.

Total Recall Bias.

Our findings suggest this probably causes a ~2pt error favoring Democrats in your standard generic ballot poll.

To add insult to injury, many pollsters are using pretty conservative weights this year. A large non-response bias amongst Republicans must occur to counteract these observations; otherwise, we are probably on track for a VA/NJ 2025 repeat.

The groups Trump made his largest gains with (younger, non-white, lower income, non-college, politically disaffected) are the most likely to lie to pollsters by saying they didn't vote for him in 2024, because they're reinforcing their upcoming vote choice.
